folds.body:
This report, full COVERAGE.json and all SA2-P1–P5 packets were read alongside the Six Ages1 tombstone and King of Dragon Pass report/coverage/packets. App2278010 and app881420 remain distinct. The retired wrong-title intake records no copied/read source and is not an active acquisition blocker; retain its tombstone and history instead of deleting it or requeueing Six Ages1. The sourcecopy/export/hash claims identify the historical finite pass, not present entitlement, installed availability or authority to uninstall. Private payloads and six named native method bodies were not reopened in this reconciliation. Scene bytecode, detailed skill/mortality rules, full succession/ventures and save encoding remain explicitly unread.

Preserve SA2-P1’s same person across age/role/availability changes; P2’s forecast before actual allocation and distinct reserve; P3’s skilled helper, repair terms and interruption settlement; P4’s coarse unseen periods/contact with one resolution; P5’s event cleanup and meaningful yearly aftermath. These are original proposed consumers, not accepted franchise mechanics or a universal neglect/aging penalty. Reuse existing actor, job, calendar, stock and history owners when a matching slice is selected; a proposed dueAt field does not call for a second job clock. Long-interval versus split-interval equivalence is a useful precise failure case, not proof every NPC needs per-tick simulation.

Packet compatibility/exclusion boilerplate is historical scope. Current old-save direction can permit reset, while newly built current state still needs its actual round trip; “no unapproved true death” does not establish a universal world mortality law. Exact private source probabilities and canon interpretations remain unknown. Related King of Dragon Pass proposals overlap on preparation, helper availability and aftermath, but retain their distinct source identity and IDs; no combined new subsystem or original experience/foundation GM lease was created.
